category: per-second Linux microVM for coding agents

free_tier.stated: Free plan: $5 of credit once per email address, with no card needed; 1 machine running at a time, 3 machines kept per workspace, each up to 2 vCPUs, 4 GiB and 20 GiB of disk, with 3 snapshots and up to 60 machines created an hour.
free_tier.notes: The $5 credit is a one-time grant per email address, not a recurring allowance. Credit does not expire. A machine suspends after 15 idle minutes on Free and only pays for disk while suspended.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a whole Firecracker microVM with a persistent /data disk; a Free-plan machine can have up to 20 GiB of disk and the universal template has no compiler, Docker or browser preinstalled

retention.stated: Everything under /data survives stops, restarts and resizes; the disk lives on one host with no automatic backups. Machines and snapshots on the welcome credit alone are deleted 7 days after a warning when unused for 14 days; credit at zero deletes everything 7 days after the warning, or 30 days if the workspace has ever paid. Command history keeps the newest 100 commands for 30 days.

egress.terms: Data out is charged per GiB by region of departure: $0.03 from North America and Europe, $0.06 from Asia-Pacific and South America, $0.18 from Africa and India; an inter-region hop is another $0.009 per GiB each way in North America and Europe. Data coming in is free, and usage is charged every ten minutes.
egress.price_per_tb: $0.03 per GiB from North America and Europe; $0.06 per GiB from Asia-Pacific and South America; $0.18 per GiB from Africa and India

interface_detail: A CLI with --json output and meaningful exit codes, a REST API with an OpenAPI 3.1 document, and a hosted MCP server with 27 tools over Streamable HTTP; TypeScript and Python SDKs exist for the API.
tooling: the user installs the quivvo CLI with npm and drives machines from the CLI, REST API or hosted MCP server; an agent with no browser can sign itself up and the owner approves it with a code.
chaining: A machine runs coding agents and keeps state on /data across stops and snapshots; published ports serve HTTPS while the machine runs, and background jobs survive a disconnect for up to 24 hours, so short agent tasks chain through the MCP server while longer servers need a separate always-on offer.

limits.value: $5 of one-time credit per email address on Free; $0.005 per vCPU-hour and $0.011 per GiB-hour while running, $0.20 per GiB-month of disk, $0.03 per GiB of data out from North America and Europe
1 machine running at a time on Free, 3 machines per workspace, largest machine 2 vCPUs and 4 GiB, up to 20 GiB disk per machine, 3 snapshots, up to 60 machines created an hour
15 idle minutes before auto-suspend on Free, and a 280-second wait-command cap with a 86400-second maximum for background jobs
long output keeps its first 256 KiB and last 768 KiB per stream with --json and without --stream; a workspace keeps the newest 8 MiB of command history and 1 MiB of feedback

limits_note: vCPUs are shared and burst to full cores before settling to a baseline if busy for long stretches. Suspended and stopped machines still pay for disk and the template system disk. A fork counts as a running machine on Free, so the source must be suspended first.
binding_note: The $5 one-time credit runs out first: a default 2 vCPU, 4 GiB machine costs $0.054 an hour while running, after which machines are suspended until the workspace is topped up.

identity_cost.detail: New accounts get $5 of credit with no card needed, once per email address; the CLI signs the user in, and an agent with no browser can sign itself up with the owner approving by a code.

reliability_note: Suspend tries to keep memory but the provider documents only up to 2 GB, so a 4 GiB machine is often stopped instead and loses in-memory processes; a host move gives a cold boot and may drop anything installed outside /data. There are no automatic backups, and credit at zero suspends machines and eventually deletes them and their snapshots.
confidence_note: Rates, plan limits, egress prices, idle suspension and the registration gate are first-party text quoted from the vendor's pricing, home, machines and agents pages read on 2026-11-24.

notes: A Firecracker microVM for coding agents, with root, a persistent /data disk, and CLI, REST and MCP access. The Free plan grants $5 once per email address with no card, runs one machine at a time up to 2 vCPUs and 4 GiB, and suspends it after 15 idle minutes. Egress is metered by departure region from $0.03 per GiB in North America and Europe.

shape.note: the default machine is 2 vCPUs and 4 GiB with a 10 GiB disk; the Free plan allows up to 20 GiB
